title: fix(discord): remove stale Working previews after repeated delete failures
body:
Related: #138630

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a stale Discord “Working” preview remaining beside the final reply when two transient DELETE requests fail during turn cleanup.

## User Impact

Progress previews are removed after transient Discord API failures recover. Error finals still retain their progress draft. Cleanup remains bounded and best effort if failures persist; no configuration or migration is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Retry the idempotent DELETE with the existing Discord retry policy while the current draft lifecycle still owns it. This replaces the proposed account-wide custody registry and detached retry machinery with the existing owner and backoff policy.

Thanks to @LiuwqGit for the original fix. Contributor commits and authorship are preserved.

Co-authored-by: LiuwqGit <liu.weiqin@xydigit.com>

## Evidence

- Strengthened the existing REST-boundary regression: two injected DELETE 503s must recover within one cleanup call. It fails against unmodified base `133b8ec1d5b2` with the preview still visible; the other 16 REST tests pass, including error-final retention. With this fix, all 17 REST tests pass, including the single-cleanup regression (12 ms) and error-final retention.
- Fixed-head real-transport proof (head `3c3db2a64c`, production controller and real RequestClient against a local Discord REST emulator — no mocked fetch, no fake timers): in one cleanup invocation the production retry policy drove DELETE 503 → 503 → 204 with real backoff (~1 s apart) and removed the preview, leaving only the delivered final reply. A separate error-final turn issued zero DELETE requests during cleanup and retained its progress draft, preserving error-final retention. The identical harness on unmodified main (`7d7cf4e07c`) leaves the stale “Working” preview visible beside the delivered answer after the same two transient DELETE failures. Reproduction script and raw terminal output: [gist](https://gist.github.com/LiuwqGit/e8a34d420ed8430ec3d2c469d81b3b60).
- No live Discord round-trip: QA broker credentials unavailable.
- Targeted typed Oxlint and Oxfmt pass. The aggregate local check reports pre-existing max-lines suppressions in three UI modules that are unchanged from the integrated main; remaining broad checks are deferred to PR CI. Independent review found no actionable P0–P2 defects.
- A real isolated Gateway using the compiled Discord plugin, the existing mock model server, and a local Discord REST/WebSocket emulator reproduced the base failure: final reply delivered, two preview DELETE 503s, then the preview still present in API history after 15 seconds.
- Compared with current main: production +4/-1 (net +3), tests +2/-5 (net -3), docs +3/-2 (net +1). The small production increase reuses the established retry policy without adding state or a new API.

The native PR checkout uses a shared installation, which refuses local declaration generation and lacks the UI-local test dependency. Focused checks run in the installed tooling checkout with byte-identical candidate files; PR CI covers the integrated tree.

**Real environment tested:** Linux (EL8) x64, Node 26.7.0; the production Discord draft preview controller and real RequestClient compiled from the checked-out trees (fixed head `3c3db2a64c`; unmodified main `7d7cf4e07c`) against a local Discord REST emulator over real HTTP — no mocked fetch, no fake timers, production retry backoff.

**Exact steps or commands run after this patch:** `PROOF_WORKTREE=<tree> node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs fixed-head-live-proof.mts` (script and raw terminal output: https://gist.github.com/LiuwqGit/e8a34d420ed8430ec3d2c469d81b3b60). Scenario A streams a progress preview, delivers a success final through the production lifecycle, then runs one `cleanup()` while the emulator answers the preview DELETE with 503, 503, then 204. Scenario B delivers an error final and runs one `cleanup()`.

**Evidence after fix:**

```text
scenario A (success final, one cleanup):
  DELETE 9000000000000000001 -> 503 at t+79ms
  DELETE 9000000000000000001 -> 503 at t+1048ms   (production backoff ~1s)
  DELETE 9000000000000000001 -> 204 at t+2050ms   (production backoff ~1s)
  visibleMessagesAfterCleanup: [ { id: 9000000000000000002, text: "Here is the final answer." } ]
scenario B (error final, one cleanup):
  deleteRequestsDuringScenario: []
  visibleMessagesAfterCleanup: [ ...final answer..., { text: "Exec: failed" }, { text: "Something failed" } ]
```

**Observed result after fix:** One cleanup invocation drove DELETE 503 → 503 → 204 through the production Discord retry policy with real backoff and removed the preview; only the delivered final reply remained. The error-final turn issued zero DELETE requests in cleanup and retained its progress draft, preserving error-final retention. The identical harness on unmodified main (`7d7cf4e07c`) leaves the stale “Working” preview visible beside the delivered answer after the same two transient DELETE failures (`discord stream preview cleanup failed: temporarily unavailable`).

**What was not tested:** A live Discord round-trip (QA broker credentials unavailable) and the cross-restart recovery case from #138630, which this partial fix intentionally does not cover.

CI on head `3c3db2a64c675e526dd516846c727be0c637813d`: [run 39559676354](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39559676354) passed changed Node tests, lint, production types, docs, and boundary checks. Test types failed in two CI-planning fixtures added by main commit `0f750efb137b2`, which is absent from this PR head but present in the CI merge (`586f3d6acca1e`). The scheduled main run at head `4fa2da58c1` (which contains `0f750efb137b2`) also fails `check-test-types-core-2` on pure main, confirming the fixture failure is main-wide and unrelated to this PR's three-file diff. No unrelated fixture repair or CI rerun is included.
